homepage_url_justification: The stable project website is https://www.quantdinger.com.
sites_https_justification: The project website, repository, documentation, and distribution endpoints use HTTPS.
description_good_justification: README.md and the project website explain that QuantDinger is an open-source AI quantitative trading operating system for research, backtesting, paper trading, and live execution.
interact_justification: README.md links installation instructions, GitHub Issues, Discussions, the contribution guide, and community channels.
contribution_justification: The contribution process is documented at https://github.com/OpenByteInc/QuantDinger/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md.
contribution_requirements_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md documents scope, coding, DCO, pull request, testing, API, and security requirements.
license_location_justification: The Apache-2.0 license is stored in the repository root LICENSE file.
floss_license_justification: QuantDinger source code is released under Apache-2.0.
floss_license_osi_justification: Apache-2.0 is approved by the Open Source Initiative.
documentation_basics_justification: README.md, DEVELOPMENT.md, deployment guides, and docs/ document installation, configuration, operation, and security.
documentation_interface_justification: Public HTTP interfaces are documented in docs/api/openapi.yaml and Agent Gateway interfaces in docs/agent/agent-openapi.json.
repo_public_justification: The source repository is publicly readable at https://github.com/OpenByteInc/QuantDinger.
repo_track_justification: Git records every change, author, committer, and timestamp in the public repository history.
repo_interim_justification: The repository publishes development history and pull requests, not only final release snapshots.
repo_distributed_justification: The project uses Git, a common distributed version control system.
version_unique_justification: Official versions use unique vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH git tags and immutable commit identifiers.
version_semver_justification: Release tags follow semantic versioning, for example v5.7.3.
version_tags_justification: Release identifiers are recorded as public git tags in the repository.
release_notes_justification: CHANGELOG.md and GitHub Releases provide functional change records; the release workflow generates notes from merged changes.
release_notes_vulns_justification: SECURITY.md and release notes identify disclosed security fixes and provide upgrade guidance when disclosure is safe.
report_url_justification: Bugs and feature requests are accepted at https://github.com/OpenByteInc/QuantDinger/issues.
report_tracker_justification: GitHub Issues publicly tracks defect and enhancement status and history.
report_process_justification: README.md, CONTRIBUTING.md, and the issue templates document how to submit useful reports.
report_responses_justification: Maintainers actively triage and respond to public issues; recent issue activity is visible in the repository.
enhancement_responses_justification: Enhancement requests are tracked through GitHub Issues, Discussions, and the public roadmap.
report_archive_justification: GitHub permanently archives closed and open issues, pull requests, and discussions.
vulnerability_report_process_justificati: SECURITY.md documents scope, private reporting, response targets, remediation targets, and coordinated disclosure.
vulnerability_report_private_justificati: SECURITY.md directs sensitive reports to support@quantdinger.com instead of a public issue.
vulnerability_report_response_justificat: SECURITY.md commits to acknowledgement within 72 hours and preliminary assessment within seven days.
build_justification: Docker Compose and Python build/install paths are exercised by GitHub Actions and documented in DEVELOPMENT.md.
build_common_tools_justification: The build uses standard FLOSS tools including Python, pip, Docker, Docker Compose, Buildx, and GitHub Actions.
build_floss_tools_justification: All tools required to build the open-source backend and MCP package are available as FLOSS.
test_justification: The repository contains extensive pytest suites for backend, integration, release-gate, OpenAPI, and MCP behavior.
test_invocation_justification: docs/getting-started/TESTING.md provides standard commands to install test dependencies and run each test suite.
test_most_justification: More than 350 public test modules cover core authentication, authorization, data, strategy, broker, API, integration, and release-gate behavior.
test_policy_justification: docs/getting-started/TESTING.md requires automated tests for major functionality and security-sensitive fixes.
tests_are_added_justification: The contribution policy requires tests for major behavior and regression tests for bug and security fixes.
tests_documented_added_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md links the mandatory test policy and requires pull requests to report verification performed.
warnings_justification: Backend CI runs Python compilation, Ruff, structure guardrails, dependency lock checks, and OpenAPI linting.
warnings_fixed_justification: Critical lint and validation findings fail CI and must be resolved before the corresponding check passes.
know_secure_design_justification: docs/security/SECURE_DEVELOPMENT.md documents least privilege, trust boundaries, input validation, credential handling, cryptography, and release controls.
know_common_errors_justification: Maintainers use CodeQL, Bandit, pip-audit, Gitleaks, security regression tests, and documented secure-development rules to address common weaknesses.
crypto_published_justification: The project uses public standard algorithms and protocols through established Python and platform libraries.
crypto_call_justification: Cryptographic operations use maintained libraries and framework APIs instead of project-designed cryptography.
crypto_floss_justification: Required cryptographic implementations are provided by FLOSS Python and operating-system libraries.
crypto_keylength_justification: Deployment documentation requires high-entropy secrets and application startup rejects missing, known-default, or undersized signing secrets.
crypto_working_justification: The default security mechanisms do not intentionally rely on MD4, MD5, DES, RC4, or other known-broken algorithms.
crypto_weaknesses_justification: The secure-development policy prohibits algorithms and modes with known serious weaknesses.
crypto_pfs_justification: QuantDinger does not implement a custom key-agreement protocol; TLS termination is provided by the deployment reverse proxy.
crypto_password_storage_justification: The standard deployment stores user passwords as adaptive salted bcrypt hashes and never as plaintext.
crypto_random_justification: Secrets and tokens use cryptographically secure randomness from Python and operating-system security APIs.
delivery_mitm_justification: Source, documentation, release metadata, and container distribution are delivered over authenticated HTTPS channels.
delivery_unsigned_justification: The project does not retrieve a hash over unauthenticated HTTP and use it as release verification; official release images are distributed over GHCR and signed by the release workflow.
vulnerabilities_fixed_60_days_justificat: SECURITY.md sets a 60-day maximum target for publicly known exploitable medium-or-higher vulnerabilities, and no such overdue issue is known.
vulnerabilities_critical_fixed_justifica: SECURITY.md sets a seven-day target for critical issues and documents prior coordinated fixes.
no_leaked_credentials_justification: Gitleaks scans full repository history; environment and backup files are ignored and only sanitized examples are committed.
static_analysis_justification: CodeQL, Bandit, and Ruff run in GitHub Actions for source changes and scheduled security checks.
static_analysis_common_vulnerabilities_j: CodeQL and Bandit include rules for common Python and application security weaknesses.
static_analysis_fixed_justification: Confirmed exploitable medium-or-higher findings are handled under the SECURITY.md remediation targets.
static_analysis_often_justification: CodeQL runs on pushes and pull requests and Security CI also runs weekly.
dynamic_analysis_justification: The project runs extensive integration and release-gate tests but has not yet established a dedicated DAST or fuzzing gate for every major release.
dynamic_analysis_unsafe_justification: The released project code is written in memory-safe or interpreted languages and does not include a maintained C or C++ codebase.
dynamic_analysis_enable_assertions_justi: Automated tests run with Python assertions enabled and exercise validation, authorization, and execution invariants.
dynamic_analysis_fixed_justification: No dedicated dynamic-analysis finding is currently outstanding; confirmed test-discovered security defects follow SECURITY.md.
test_continuous_integration_justificatio: GitHub Actions runs automated tests for pushes and pull requests to the default branch.
discussion_justification: GitHub Issues, Discussions, and pull requests provide public mechanisms for usage questions and proposed changes.
english_justification: The primary README, contribution, governance, security, architecture, API, testing, and release documentation is available in English.
hardening_justification: The project provides a production hardening Compose override, least-privilege workflow permissions, process isolation, strict secret validation, and deployment security guidance.
crypto_used_network_justification: Public deployments are documented to use HTTPS/TLS and external providers use HTTPS endpoints by default.
crypto_tls12_justification: Supported production deployments terminate HTTPS with modern reverse proxies and require TLS 1.2 or newer for public access.
crypto_certificate_verification_justific: Outbound HTTPS clients use normal certificate verification by default; disabling verification is not a supported default.
crypto_verification_private_justificatio: TLS certificate verification occurs before authenticated headers or provider credentials are transmitted.
installation_common_justification: Users install and remove QuantDinger using standard Docker Compose or documented Python package tooling.
maintained_justification: The repository has frequent commits, issue activity, security fixes, tagged versions, and an active public roadmap.
OSPS-AC-04.01_justification: Every GitHub Actions workflow defines explicit read-only top-level permissions; individual jobs elevate only the permissions required for publishing or security uploads.
OSPS-BR-02.01_justification: Official releases use unique semantic version tags such as v5.7.3 and immutable commit identifiers.
OSPS-BR-04.01_justification: CHANGELOG.md records release policy and security changes, and the release workflow generates descriptive GitHub release notes.
OSPS-BR-05.01_justification: Build and release pipelines use standardized pip, Docker Buildx, GHCR, GitHub Releases, and Sigstore tooling.
OSPS-BR-06.01_justification: The release workflow publishes SBOM and provenance attestations and signs the immutable backend image digest using Sigstore keyless signing.
OSPS-DO-06.01_justification: docs/security/DEPENDENCY_POLICY.md documents dependency selection, declaration, locking, monitoring, and release treatment.
OSPS-DO-07.01_justification: DEVELOPMENT.md and README.md document source and container builds, required libraries, frameworks, services, and development dependencies.
OSPS-GV-01.01_justification: MAINTAINERS.md publicly lists the project member with repository administration, release, package, and security-report access.
OSPS-GV-01.02_justification: GOVERNANCE.md defines Project Lead, Maintainer, and Contributor roles and their responsibilities.
OSPS-GV-03.02_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md defines acceptable contribution scope, coding, DCO, pull request, testing, API, and security requirements.
OSPS-LE-01.01_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md requires a Developer Certificate of Origin Signed-off-by trailer on every commit and the DCO workflow rejects unsigned pull-request commits.
OSPS-QA-03.01_justification: The default-branch ruleset requires configured GitHub Actions status checks to pass before merge, with bypass reserved for explicitly recorded emergencies.
OSPS-QA-06.01_justification: Backend, MCP, OpenAPI, security, and release checks run automatically on pull requests; required checks must pass before the default branch accepts a change.
OSPS-SA-01.01_justification: docs/security/SECURITY_ASSESSMENT.md lists actors, actions, boundaries, risks, and controls and links the full architecture documentation.
OSPS-SA-02.01_justification: External HTTP interfaces are documented in docs/api/openapi.yaml and docs/agent/agent-openapi.json; broker and deployment interfaces are documented under docs/.
OSPS-SA-03.01_justification: docs/security/SECURITY_ASSESSMENT.md assesses likely high-impact risks including credentials, authorization, strategy execution, SSRF, orders, supply chain, tenant isolation, and AI actions.
OSPS-VM-01.01_justification: SECURITY.md defines coordinated disclosure, acknowledgement and assessment times, severity-based remediation targets, public disclosure, and reporter credit.
OSPS-VM-03.01_justification: SECURITY.md provides support@quantdinger.com for private vulnerability reports and explicitly prohibits public vulnerability issues.
OSPS-VM-04.01_justification: Resolved vulnerabilities and operator guidance are publicly documented in SECURITY.md and applicable GitHub release notes or security advisories.
